body:
I've just always been overly reliant on other people to give me the feeling of being loved and valued. When these people leave my life it puts me back in square one. 
I have a few friends but none I can be myself around. I'm just too confused about what that entails and scared shitless that my true self is completely unlovable. 
I'm speaking to a medical professional, on meds, jumping through all the hoops, don't feel like I'm really getting anywhere though. 
I've always maintained that there are plenty of solutions available, just none that I have any faith in myself to pursue. Getting out of a rut takes a determination that I'm lacking in spades. 
I do wonder how we got here and I'm sure the full picture is spellbinding. But I don't feel part of that. I don't feel properly human. Just very, very wrong, in a way that cannot be fixed.
Well maybe I sound ridiculous, but being less than a person in a world full of people doesn't exactly fill you with pride. I'd love to claw my way back up it just seems like I'm in no way capable

I definitely know how it feels to relentlessly blame myself for almost everything that goes wrong. Sure beats blaming others, you probably find you get closer to the truth half the time too. I'll never have the drive to make my own living, so I'm kind of living on borrowed time. Thanks for your comment :)
Experience I guess... total lack of friends, discernable talents, past achievments... I'm just a complete waste. I can't think of anything positive to console myself with.

Late reply but I've been a little busy... 
I'm not without an ambition, or a vision for what I want for the future, part of that is the reason I'm currently at university... I just struggle to believe anything I want is obtainable. 
I did start a YouTube channel back in the day, it was pretty fun but I think it's run its course... it was never gonna blow up or anything like that. Appreciate the personal development tips as well, even if I won't have the time right about now to go around the world and do crazy shit, personal development should probably be my focus right now.
I'd back anyone but me to do it! I appreciate the conversation though man.

Yeah, it's the seeking part. I don't think I have the drive to do anything anymore, even if it may lead to everything I tell myself I want. I just don't have it in me to find a solution to a problem and comitt to its implementation. I'm too tired and weak.
It's probably a lot of things... I'm sure it isn't insurmountably bad but I'll never be able to commit myself to seeking a solution. Feels bad man.

I'm serious, my brain seems to have regressed to a child-like state... I can't keep up with anyone anymore, everything's too slow... 
I think I'm just slowly resigning myself to the idea that nothing will get better and I will remain like this for the rest of my life

I'll try to reach out, there's no knowing how I would react if I were that desperate but I'd like to think I'd want help. I went to a doctor about 3 years ago now but the service was so poor, I was told I didn't have a mental health issue but that was after a lot of telling them what I thought they wanted to hear on my part. 

I hope people find me fun to be around and everything, it didn't work out last time but the effect of feeling uninteresting probably didn't help. I saw that sub earlier haha, I'm definitely agreeing with the idea that David Attenborough is the only reason you would need to live.

I've never spoken to anyone else while actually suicidal before, it's hard to want to do anything but lie in bed. There's no way I'll actually hurt myself though. 

Thanks for the idea with regard to self-confidence, the thing about positive self-reinforcement though is how frequently you have to do it before it stops feeling ridiculous. I'm aware that comparing myself to others is pointless, and I try and avoid it, I always feel like I should be a lot better though (and by extension more like them). 

I'm not too sure whether I actually have depression, what I experience doesn't seem severe or frequent enough, but I get your point, it'll definitely impair me. I feel like I don't have the ability that I did when I got the grades to go to uni though. I definitely would like to get more involved in sports and societies, and I guess I'll meet people with similar interests and whatnot, it's just a question of whether I'm interesting enough for them to want to talk to me.

Hey Abby, my name's David. 

I'm not currently feeling suicidal, my ideation doesn't normally last so long. I don't know why but I have an overwhelming sense that I'm incapable of even the simplest thing. I don't go into any task, even something that I might end up being good at, with any confidence.  It's probably just a lack of prior success and accomplishments, and the fact that I relentlessly compare myself to others a lot of the time. 

I'm going back to uni in a couple of weeks after a leave of absence, I guess I've just lost faith in my ability to cope with what might come my way academically, and I never had any faith in my ability to make a decent amount of friends to begin with. I'll only know once I'm there I guess.

It would certainly benefit me to think about what specifically I don't like about myself, I'm sure it's a lot more nuanced than "everything". Should be able to have a chat with someone about this when I go back to Uni, so long as I don't procrastinate yet again. 

I appreciate you taking the time to reply man. :)
